pci_irq_entry.status: source-verified interrupt numbering, index selection, handler context and teardown ordering; physical delivery unverified
pci_irq_entry.route: i915 request_irq(pdev->irq) -> linuxkpi irq lookup -> bus_setup_intr -> nmx_xnu_pci_irq_setup -> IOInterruptEventSource on its own IOWorkLoop -> intr_trampoline -> i915 handler

verified.edge: irq numbering agrees between pci_alloc_msi, the resource and the requested irq
anchors: port: bsdcompat/src/nmx_bus.c:96-100,138 each PCI function owns a block of IRQ_BLOCK (64) numbers from IRQ_FIRST (1024): base + 0 is the legacy line, base + n is message-signalled vector n-1
port: bsdcompat/src/nmx_bus.c:810-815 bus_alloc_resource maps rid 0 to the legacy line and rid n to vector n-1, setting r->irqno = irq_base + rid
port: override/src/linux_pci.c:1603-1606 after pci_alloc_msi the device's irq becomes rid 1's start, i.e. the first message-signalled vector
drm: i915_irq.c:1215,1227 intel_irq_install requests exactly to_pci_dev(...)->irq
verified.finding: pdev->irq, the resource irqno and the vector index the IOKit lookup will pick all derive from the same rid, so the handler cannot be attached to a different vector than the one the device was granted. Legacy keeps base + 0 and is selected by vector < 0.

verified.edge: vector index translates to an IOKit interrupt index
anchors: port: xnu/nmx_pci.cpp:117-133 interrupt_index walks getInterruptType, counts message-signalled entries and returns the n-th of them, or the first legacy entry when vector < 0
verified.finding: The count reported by pci_msi_count and the index chosen at setup use the same walk, so the n-th enabled vector is the n-th message-signalled entry. pci_msix_count returns 0 (nmx_bus.c:996), so i915's single-vector request takes the MSI path rather than MSI-X.

verified.edge: the driver handler runs on a work-loop thread, not in primary interrupt context
anchors: port: xnu/nmx_pci.cpp:98-114 an NMXIrq owner keeps the handler and arg; IOInterruptEventSource dispatches irq_action on the loop
port: xnu/nmx_pci.cpp:168-181 one IOWorkLoop per vector, event source added, then enabled
drm: i915_irq.c:1227 i915 registers a single non-threaded handler with IRQF_SHARED
verified.finding: This differs from a hard-IRQ handler but matches what i915 needs: no threaded split, no sleeping in the handler beyond what the uncore waits already do, and the interrupt line is masked by IOKit while the action runs. The cost is latency, not correctness, and that cost is a target question.

verified.edge: the trampoline keeps FreeBSD filter/handler semantics
anchors: port: bsdcompat/src/nmx_bus.c:848-856 rv defaults to FILTER_SCHEDULE_THREAD; the filter, when present, runs first and the handler runs only if the filter still asks for the thread
verified.finding: For i915, which passes no filter, the handler always runs. A filter that returns FILTER_HANDLED suppresses the handler as FreeBSD specifies. What does not happen is running the filter in interrupt context; on this port both run on the loop thread.

verified.edge: teardown cannot free the callback out from under an in-flight interrupt
anchors: port: xnu/nmx_pci.cpp:225-236 teardown disables the event source, runs a drain action on the loop (which waits for any running action to finish), removes the event source, then releases event source, loop and owner in that order
port: bsdcompat/src/nmx_bus.c:884-895 bus_teardown_intr unlinks the cookie under the list lock, tears down the native interrupt, then frees the cookie
port: bsdcompat/src/nmx_bus.c:729-745 _intr_drain retains each work loop while the list lock is held, so a concurrent teardown cannot free the loop mid-drain
verified.finding: The ordering is remove-after-drain-then-free at every level, and the object the action dereferences stays alive until the drain returns.

verified.edge: a latent out-of-bounds in the pinned dependency is not reachable here
anchors: freebsd: sys/compat/linuxkpi/common/src/linux_pci.c:1433-1438 and the port's copy at override/src/linux_pci.c:1671-1676 compute vec = irq_start - irq, which is <= 0 for every irq >= irq_start, then index msi_desc[vec]
freebsd: sys/compat/linuxkpi/common/include/linux/interrupt.h:143-148 the only caller path is irq_get_msi_desc(irq)
grep over the pinned DRM tree and the port: no caller of irq_get_msi_desc
verified.finding: The expression is inverted (it should be irq - irq_start) and would index msi_desc[] negatively for any vector past the first. It is upstream code, it is unreachable in this build because irq_get_msi_desc has no callers, and it is recorded rather than patched so the dependency stays as pinned.

close_path.status: source-verified probe teardown, cdev close ordering, per-mapping release order and the RCU callback; no target evidence
close_path.route: probe scope exit -> Buffer/Program/Context destructors -> process exit -> nmx_close -> nmx_cdev_close -> umap_release_all -> fdrop -> linux_file_close -> drm_release -> linux_synchronize_rcu

verified.edge: the probe destroys in dependency order, enforced by scope rather than by hand
anchors: probe: main.cpp:459-461 run() declares the two buffers first and Program after them, so Program is destroyed first
probe: main.cpp:437-446 ~Program destroys fence, command pool, descriptor pool, pipeline, shader module, pipeline layout, descriptor set layout in that order
probe: main.cpp:371-376 ~Buffer unmaps, destroys the buffer, then frees the memory
probe: main.cpp:190-195 ~Context destroys the device, then the debug messenger, then the instance
probe: main.cpp:601-607 main() declares Deadline, then Library, then Context, so Context dies before dlclose and the deadline stays armed through teardown
verified.finding: Descriptors are gone before the buffers they name, the device is gone before the loader handle, and the deadline covers teardown so a hang is reported rather than hanging the machine silently.

verified.edge: every iteration completes before anything is destroyed
anchors: probe: main.cpp:552-556 a fence result other than VK_SUCCESS abandons teardown with _Exit(124 on timeout, 2 otherwise) instead of destroying possibly in-flight resources
probe: main.cpp:557-563 the readback is compared only after that wait, and a mismatch throws, which unwinds through the ordered destructors
verified.finding: Normal teardown only ever runs after the GPU work completed and was read back. The _Exit paths are failure policy, not cleanup, so a failure run does not double as evidence of clean teardown.

verified.edge: user mappings are released before the file release
anchors: port: override/src/nmx_linux_cdev.c:357-384 nmx_cdev_close unlinks the open under opens_mtx, then calls umap_release_all(o), then runs the driver close and fdrop, then devfs_clear_cdevpriv, dev_rel, destroy and free
verified.finding: The native user mapping teardown happens strictly before the file's release path can drop the last GEM/VM references.

verified.edge: each mapping is unwound unmap -> unpin -> vma close -> file/mm put
anchors: port: override/src/nmx_linux_cdev.c:531-547 umap_free calls nmx_xnu_unmap_user, then the pin callback with false, then vma->vm_ops->close, then fput(vma->vm_file), then mmput(vma->vm_mm), then frees
port: override/src/nmx_linux_cdev.c:646-660 umap_release_all pops each record under maps_mtx and frees it outside the lock, so no sleeping free happens under the mutex
verified.finding: This is the order T7 asks for: native unmap first, unpin second, and only then the vma close that releases the GEM object and the file/mm references.

verified.edge: the close-path RCU wait no longer takes the thread registry lock
anchors: port: override/src/linux_compat.c:1146-1185 linux_file_close runs the driver release, drops the fops/cdev references, then calls linux_synchronize_rcu(RCU_TYPE_REGULAR) and only then frees the file
port: override/src/linux_rcu.c:213-221 the grace-period callback is now just pause("nmxrcu", 1); it does not call nmx_curthread or take any registry lock
port: override/src/linux_rcu.c:72 RCU_SKIP() compiles to 0 in this build, so the wait is not skipped
ck: ck_epoch_synchronize_wait invokes the callback through epoch_block (freebsd ck_epoch.c:411-419), which holds no ck lock while calling it
r14: panic-2026-10-21-183746.txt shows the old stack linux_synchronize_rcu_cb -> nmx_curthread -> nmx_thread_get -> IOSimpleLockLock, ending in a TLB-shootdown timeout
verified.finding: The r14 stack spent the grace period spinning inside the thread-registry simple lock, which is exactly the shape that starves a TLB shootdown. Today the callback sleeps outside every lock, so that mechanism is gone from source. This does not prove the close path is safe on the target, only that the specific r14 mechanism is no longer present.

verified.edge: failure modes are separated instead of sharing one path
anchors: probe: main.cpp:548-551 submit failure exits 2 without teardown
probe: main.cpp:553-556 fence timeout exits 124, other fence errors exit 2
probe: main.cpp:106-118 the overall deadline, which includes teardown, exits 124
probe: main.cpp:563 a readback mismatch throws and unwinds normally
verified.finding: Normal exit, compute error, submit failure, wait timeout and deadline expiry are distinguishable from the exit code and the last printed stage, which is what T7 asks to be recorded separately.
